articles.title: OTA Updates Are Easy. That's Why They Brick Your Fleet.
articles.excerpt: How dual-slot bootloaders, the confirm/revert lifecycle, and a monotonic counter turn "works on my bench" into "survives the field." Most firmware engineers get the OTA upload working on the first or…
articles.body: How dual-slot bootloaders, the confirm/revert lifecycle, and a monotonic counter turn "works on my bench" into "survives the field." Most firmware engineers get the OTA upload working on the first or second try. The image transfers, the device reboots, the new firmware runs. Then a week later a buggy build ships over the air, the device crashes in a loop, and the only recovery is a truck roll. The upload was never the hard part. The rollback is. This post is the pipeline the tutorials skip: how MCUboot's swap-and-confirm lifecycle and ESP-IDF's dual-partition OTA actually protect you, where each one silently fails, and the one test that tells you whether your rollback works before your fleet finds out for you.

articles.title: ReTrace: Distilling Agent Workflows into Planner-Free Code
articles.excerpt: LLM agents can follow a Standard Operating Procedure written in natural language, but they call an inference endpoint at every decision point. That works for one-off tasks. When you run the same SOP a…
articles.body: LLM agents can follow a Standard Operating Procedure written in natural language, but they call an inference endpoint at every decision point. That works for one-off tasks. When you run the same SOP a thousand times a day, the per-step latency and token cost becomes a production problem. ReTrace solves this by tracing agent execution, extracting the decision logic from reasoning traces, and compiling a planner-free workflow. The workflow is deterministic code that selects the next tool call without an LLM in the loop. On production SOPs, ReTrace workflows reach 93.8% completion at 24% lower cost per task. On τ²-Bench, they run in 1.3 seconds instead of 170 seconds.

articles.title: Vibe Coding Built My Web App in 2 Hours. Software Engineering Is What Will Keep It Alive.
articles.excerpt: I opened VS Code, typed a prompt into an AI, and in 2 hours I had a full Web App. Campus Biz Hub. A beautiful, colorful dashboard. Students could buy, sellers could sell, admins could approve. It had…
articles.body: I opened VS Code, typed a prompt into an AI, and in 2 hours I had a full Web App. Campus Biz Hub. A beautiful, colorful dashboard. Students could buy, sellers could sell, admins could approve. It had gradients, emojis, cards, login screens. It looked like a real startup. I felt unstoppable. Then I tried to show it to my friend. Failed to resolve import "./components/Business Dashboard" Then MySQL said: Access denied for user 'and '@'localhost' Then I realized I had no real login. Anyone could click "Login" and enter. No database. No password. No security. That is vibe coding. And that is the danger. What is Vibe Coding? Vibe coding is when you build by feeling, not by engineering. You prompt: "Make it colorful, make it like the one I showed you. "AI gives you code. You paste it. It works.

articles.title: Dark matter breakthrough coming? Euclid space telescope unveils its 1st look into the dark universe (video)
articles.excerpt: The Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons.
articles.body: On Thursday (Nov. 12), the Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons. The data release lays the foundation for one of the largest-ever 3D maps of the cosmos and many groundbreaking discoveries about the nature of dark energy and dark matter. The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has been called the "Dark Universe Detective" because of its capability to investigate the dual mysteries of dark matter , the universe's most mysterious stuff, and dark energy , the force accelerating the expansion of the universe. Collectively, these cosmic elements are sometimes referred to as the dark universe.
